title: Streaming prefix-split-fanout metering validation
creator: Nina Zhang
description:
Summary:
We are seeing intermittent discrepancies between recorded token usage in the billing pipeline and runtime logs for requests that traverse the proxy layer and/or use streaming. Early investigation shows two distinct root causes that can interact: (1) prefix-splitting behavior in the streaming assembler can attribute input tokens to both the initial request and resumed fragments during reconnection, and (2) upstream proxy/load-balancer fan-out (replicas/timeouts leading to duplicated upstream fetches) can result in duplicated metering events when metering is applied at the edge rather than after de-duplication. Both issues cause customer-visible overcharging or mismatched quota enforcement. This ticket scopes a full validation, fixes, and test plan to ensure correct per-request, per-direction (input/output) token accounting across proxies, streaming resumes, and fanout scenarios.

Goals:
- Reproduce deterministic failures in CI for the two failure modes described (prefix split double-attribution; proxy-induced duplicate metering).
- Decide and implement the canonical metering point (recommended: centralized aggregator post-de-duplication/prefix-join) and patch runtime/proxy hooks accordingly.
- Add unit/e2e tests and a synthetic workload harness to catch regressions.
- Implement compensating reconciliation jobs for customers impacted in the last 90 days if we confirm double-counts.

Scope/Non-goals:
- Scope: runtime streaming assembler, proxy metering hooks, metering pipeline dedupe stage, e2e tests, rollout strategy, customer reconciliation plan.
- Non-goal: redesign of billing invoice format or pricing model.

Technical notes:
- Streaming assembly currently emits token events on each chunk emission and on resume events. When a client reconnects and the server performs prefix-split to resend the last N tokens, both the original and resumed chunk events are attributed separately. Add an idempotency token or per-request stream-sequence that the metering-aggregator uses to dedupe.
- Proxy fanout: some ALB/ingress retries generate parallel requests (race) to different backend replicas. Edge metering (metering at ingress) counts each parallel attempt. Proposed fix: attach a stable request-id from the edge and only count the first successful completion; or move metering post-failover/dedupe at the aggregator where request completion semantics are known.
- Quota enforcement currently checks tokens consumed at the API-gateway level and blocks when exceeded. If metering is moved downstream, enforce a lightweight optimistic quota check at the gateway but reconcile/lookahead at the aggregator to avoid premature rejections or double-charges.

Acceptance criteria (pass conditions):
acceptance_criteria: CI reproducer that simulates: (a) client reconnects/resumes with prefix-split and (b) proxy parallel retry/fanout; tests must assert single token attribution per logical request.
Patch merged that prevents double-counting for prefix-split resumes (idempotency or stream-sequence based dedupe).
Proxy/integration change ensuring only a single metering record per stable request-id is recorded for fanout/retry cases, with tests exercising ALB-like retry patterns.
End-to-end e2e job demonstrating no net difference between runtime token logs and billing pipeline aggregate under 10k synthetic streamed requests (95th percentile drift < 0.1%).
Rollout plan documented with canary (10% traffic) and automatic rollback trigger if billing delta > 1% on canary within 24h.
Customer reconciliation plan drafted and exec-approved if historical double-counting is confirmed (script + PRD link).
implementation_notes: Add stream_sequence and per-chunk sequence numbers to the streaming protocol (backwards compatible with clients that don't send them).
Introduce aggregator-level dedupe window keyed by (customer_id, request_id, stream_sequence) with TTL configurable per-tenant.
Edge gateway to emit stable x-rw-request-id header; metering at gateway should mark attempt but not finalize charge until aggregator confirmation.
Update quota flow: optimistic reserve at gateway (cheap token debit) and finalize on aggregator success; on duplicate attempts aggregator must release duplicates to avoid double reserve failures.
Performance: keep dedupe store in memory with LRU and graceful degradation to sampling for very high cardinality workloads to avoid increased latency.
Add feature flag `dedupe-metering-v2` for staged rollout and A/B testing on dedicated customers.
test_plan: Unit tests for stream_sequence-based dedupe logic with edge cases: out-of-order chunks, overlapping prefixes, resume-after-long-gap.
Integration test that spins up proxy replica set, simulates parallel retries and verifies a single metering event stored.
Load test harness (k6) that simulates 10k concurrent streaming sessions with random reconnects; assert billing delta thresholds.
Regression test added to metering CI to run reproducer daily under `billing-smoke` suite.
Manual QA checklist for SRE: validate canary logs, billing delta dashboard, and reconciliation dry-run on staging.
rollout_plan: Deploy dedupe aggregator to staging, run k6 load tests for 48h.
Enable feature flag for 5% of production traffic for customers with low risk profiles.
Monitor billing-delta and token-rate metrics; promote to 25% then 100% when delta < 0.25% for 72h.
If delta spikes, roll back to previous aggregator and open incident for immediate mitigation.
post_mortem_action_items: Run history-scan to identify potential duplicate charges in the last 90 days and flag accounts with >1% delta.
Prepare a customer communications template and credits policy for confirmed duplicate-charge cases.
Add observability: per-request dedupe counters, sample traces for resumed streams, and proxy-retry attribution logs.
Schedule a cross-team review with SRE/Networking/Payments to align on long-term quota enforcement architecture.
